Drawing inspiration from Monte Carlo Dropout techniques in medical imaging uncertainty quantification [Gal and Ghahramani, 2016], we propose UG-CPPO (Uncertainty-Gated CVaR-PPO), a novel architecture that dynamically gates LLM signal infusion based on prompt-ensemble-derived uncertainty. Existing market mechanisms rarely solve this tension among efficiency, agility, and privacy. We address this challenge by designing and evaluating an agent-to-agent negotiation framework for multi-issue bilateral exchange. In our setting, autonomous buyer and seller agents hold heterogeneous private preferences and learn adaptive bargaining strategies through self-play reinforcement learning under two-sided incomplete information.
